realBugFoundAndFixedByThisWork.location: bot/webpublish.js publishSite() step 6b (F3/F5/F6 post-deploy origin correction)
realBugFoundAndFixedByThisWork.description: Before this fix, section 6b unconditionally rewrote seo.canonical/og:url/robots.txt/sitemap.xml from the pre-deploy predicted origin back to the raw deploy() return url whenever they differed. That was correct for its original purpose (PENDING_SEO_ORIGIN placeholder -> real host once known) but silently undid an ACTIVE custom domain on every republish, since the underlying Cloudflare Pages deploy call always returns the Hidook subdomain/pages.dev host, never the custom domain. Fixed by gating the whole correction block on `seoBuildOrigin === PENDING_SEO_ORIGIN` — it now only fires for its original purpose, never for a deliberately-predicted origin (BRAND_DOMAIN, isolated, or an active custom domain).

whatTheStubCouldNotExpress: Real Cloudflare Pages custom-hostname A/AAAA fallback IPs for an apex domain without Cloudflare-managed DNS — that requires a live 'Cloudflare for SaaS' account and the values are account-specific; this codebase instead targets the domain's www subdomain (CNAME-able everywhere) and asks the owner to add an apex->www forwarding rule at their registrar. See HANDOFF-domains.md section 3.

Cloudflare's exact live Pages custom-domain status enum (pending/pending_deployment/initializing/verifying/...) was not verified against a real account; mapCloudflareStatus() defaults anything not explicitly active/deactivated/blocked/error to 'provisioning', which is the safe default either way.

Real-world DNS propagation timing (minutes to ~48h in rare cases) cannot be sped up or simulated meaningfully; the fake resolver in tests answers instantly, and the product copy is written to make waiting read as normal regardless of how long it actually takes.
seoOriginConsistency: bot/webpublish.js#predictedPublicOrigin(slug, {siteId}) now checks domains.getActiveDomainForSite(siteId) FIRST, before BRAND_DOMAIN/isolated-deploy formulas. Both publish-time paths (the pre-deploy seo.canonical/robots/sitemap generation AND the pre-deploy og:image absolutization) call it with the same {siteId}, so a single source of truth decides the origin every time a site is built or rebuilt. bot/site-export.js (offline ZIP/HTML export) already reused whatever seo.canonical ends up saved in config.json — since applyCustomDomainOrigin() forces that field to the real value on every connect/disconnect transition, a fresh export taken any time after picks up the correct origin automatically with no separate wiring needed there.
